      "nets": ["NET0012", "NET0006"],
      "observed": "The 6-pin AVR-ISP header's reset pin (J7 pin 5, drawn as 'RST') is wired to net NET0012 - the same net as the ATtiny PB3/XTAL1 pins (U4 pin 3, U1 pin 3) and the J6 'POT' wiper - while the ATtiny RESET/PB5 pin (U4/U1 pin 1) sits on a different net, NET0006, whose only other connection is the R7 10k pull-up. The ISP MISO/MOSI/SCK pins are correctly on NET0010 (PB1), NET0003 (PB0) and NET0007 (PB2), so only the reset line is wrong.",
      "expected": "ISP pin 5 (~RST) must be tied to the ATtiny RESET/PB5 pin (net NET0006 at U4/U1 pin 1); the potentiometer wiper should remain on PB3 (ADC3) only. The ISP reset line must be able to drive the MCU's reset pin low.",
      "evidence": [
        {"source": "schematic", "quote": "J7 AVR-ISP-6: 'MISO'->NET0010, 'MOSI'->NET0003, 'SCK'->NET0007, 'RST'->NET0012 (sheet 1, middle)"},
        {"source": "schematic", "quote": "U4 ATtiny45-20P: pin 3 'XTAL1/PB3' -> NET0012; pin 1 'RESET/PB5' -> NET0006 (sheet 1, right)"},
        {"source": "schematic", "quote": "J6 'POT' middle pin -> NET0012 (sheet 1, top right)"}
      ],
      "impact": "The programmer can never pull the ATtiny reset pin low, so in-system programming fails (the chip never enters serial programming mode); in addition the potentiometer wiper / PB3 line is shorted to the ISP reset line, so the pot reading is disturbed whenever a programmer is attached.",
      "confidence": 0.5
    },
    {
      "category": "wrong_rating",
      "components": ["R7", "R9", "U2"],
      "pins": ["R7.1", "R9.1", "U2.3", "U4.1", "U4.2", "U1.1", "U1.2"],
      "nets": ["VCC", "+5V", "NET0006", "NET0008"],
      "observed": "Both MCU-side pull-ups are returned to the VCC rail: R7 (10k) pulls up NET0006 (ATtiny RESET/PB5, U4/U1 pin 1) and R9 (10k) pulls up NET0008 (ATtiny PB4, U4/U1 pin 2, fan tach input). VCC is the pre-regulated input rail - it is the pin U2 (LM1117-5.0) takes as VI (pin 3), while U2's VO (pin 2) is +5V and is what supplies the MCU VCC pins (U4/U1 pin 8).",
      "expected": "The RESET and tach pull-ups should be returned to +5V, the regulated rail that powers the ATtiny, so that no MCU pin is pulled above its supply. A 5V logic pin must not be pulled to the raw fan/input rail.",
      "evidence": [
        {"source": "schematic", "quote": "U2 LM1117-5.0: VI = VCC, VO = +5V, GND = GND (sheet 1, right)"},
        {"source": "schematic", "quote": "U4/U1 'VCC' pin 8 tied to +5V (sheet 1, right)"},
        {"source": "schematic", "quote": "R7 10k and R9 10k tops tied to the 'VCC' symbols (sheet 1, top right)"}
      ],
      "impact": "The ATtiny's RESET/PB5 and PB4 pins are held at the raw input potential (the LM1117-5.0 only makes sense with an input above ~6.5V, e.g. a 12V fan supply), exceeding the device absolute maximum (VCC+0.5V = 5.5V); this can damage the pins, hold the part out of reset unpredictably, and make the fan-tach input permanently read high.",
      "confidence": 0.38
    }
  ],
  "summary": "The drawing contains deviations from sound design: the AVR-ISP header's RST pin is tied to the PB3/XTAL1 net (NET0012, shared with the pot wiper) instead of the ATtiny RESET/PB5 net (NET0006), which would make the board unprogrammable, and the two 10k MCU-side pull-ups (R7 on RESET, R9 on PB4/tach) are returned to the unregulated VCC input rail rather than the +5V rail that powers the ATtiny."
}

anomalies.observed: The 6-pin AVR-ISP header's reset pin (J7 pin 5, drawn as 'RST') is wired to net NET0012 - the same net as the ATtiny PB3/XTAL1 pins (U4 pin 3, U1 pin 3) and the J6 'POT' wiper - while the ATtiny RESET/PB5 pin (U4/U1 pin 1) sits on a different net, NET0006, whose only other connection is the R7 10k pull-up. The ISP MISO/MOSI/SCK pins are correctly on NET0010 (PB1), NET0003 (PB0) and NET0007 (PB2), so only the reset line is wrong.
anomalies.expected: ISP pin 5 (~RST) must be tied to the ATtiny RESET/PB5 pin (net NET0006 at U4/U1 pin 1); the potentiometer wiper should remain on PB3 (ADC3) only. The ISP reset line must be able to drive the MCU's reset pin low.

evidence.quote: U4 ATtiny45-20P: pin 3 'XTAL1/PB3' -> NET0012; pin 1 'RESET/PB5' -> NET0006 (sheet 1, right)
J6 'POT' middle pin -> NET0012 (sheet 1, top right)

anomalies.impact: The programmer can never pull the ATtiny reset pin low, so in-system programming fails (the chip never enters serial programming mode); in addition the potentiometer wiper / PB3 line is shorted to the ISP reset line, so the pot reading is disturbed whenever a programmer is attached.

anomalies.observed: Both MCU-side pull-ups are returned to the VCC rail: R7 (10k) pulls up NET0006 (ATtiny RESET/PB5, U4/U1 pin 1) and R9 (10k) pulls up NET0008 (ATtiny PB4, U4/U1 pin 2, fan tach input). VCC is the pre-regulated input rail - it is the pin U2 (LM1117-5.0) takes as VI (pin 3), while U2's VO (pin 2) is +5V and is what supplies the MCU VCC pins (U4/U1 pin 8).
anomalies.expected: The RESET and tach pull-ups should be returned to +5V, the regulated rail that powers the ATtiny, so that no MCU pin is pulled above its supply. A 5V logic pin must not be pulled to the raw fan/input rail.

evidence.quote: U2 LM1117-5.0: VI = VCC, VO = +5V, GND = GND (sheet 1, right)
R7 10k and R9 10k tops tied to the 'VCC' symbols (sheet 1, top right)

anomalies.impact: The ATtiny's RESET/PB5 and PB4 pins are held at the raw input potential (the LM1117-5.0 only makes sense with an input above ~6.5V, e.g. a 12V fan supply), exceeding the device absolute maximum (VCC+0.5V = 5.5V); this can damage the pins, hold the part out of reset unpredictably, and make the fan-tach input permanently read high.

parsed.summary: The drawing contains deviations from sound design: the AVR-ISP header's RST pin is tied to the PB3/XTAL1 net (NET0012, shared with the pot wiper) instead of the ATtiny RESET/PB5 net (NET0006), which would make the board unprogrammable, and the two 10k MCU-side pull-ups (R7 on RESET, R9 on PB4/tach) are returned to the unregulated VCC input rail rather than the +5V rail that powers the ATtiny.
